Arch: install a package, remove it (with orphaned deps), full system upgrade?
column2:
sudo pacman -S <pkg>       # install (from repos)
sudo pacman -Rns <pkg>     # remove + orphaned deps + leftover config
sudo pacman -Syu           # sync db + full upgrade (the apt update && upgrade)

apt -> pacman: install=-S, remove=-R, update+upgrade=-Syu, search=-Ss

column1: pacman: force-remove a package ignoring dependency checks (e.g. swapping a conflicting build)?
column2:
sudo pacman -Rdd <pkg>

-Rdd skips BOTH dep checks (won't complain that things need it) and
removing deps. Use when replacing immediately, e.g. repo wezterm -> nightly:
  sudo pacman -Rdd wezterm && paru -S wezterm-nightly-bin

column1: pacman: search repos, list installed matches, check one package is installed?
column2:
pacman -Ss <term>    # search available packages (repos only)
pacman -Qs <term>    # search INSTALLED packages
pacman -Q  <pkg>     # is exactly this installed? (exit 0 / prints version)

Q = query local db, S = sync (remote) db.

column1: pacman: stop a package from being upgraded (pin an old version)?
column2:
# /etc/pacman.conf, under [options]:
IgnorePkg = amneziavpn-bin

Syu then skips it. Space-separate multiple names, or list-line them.

column1: What is the AUR, and how does an AUR install differ from a repo package?
column2:
AUR = Arch User Repository: community BUILD RECIPES (PKGBUILD), not prebuilt
binaries. A helper (paru) downloads the PKGBUILD, builds locally, hands the
result to pacman. Repo packages are prebuilt + signed.

Because recipes are user-submitted, paru shows you the PKGBUILD to REVIEW
before building -- that's the security step, not ceremony. `-bin` packages
just fetch the upstream binary, so their PKGBUILD is short.

column1: paru -Ss vs pacman -Ss? And where does paru come from on CachyOS?
column2:
paru -Ss <term>   # searches official repos AND the AUR
pacman -Ss <term> # official repos only

paru is an AUR HELPER (wrapper around pacman). On CachyOS it's in the repos:
  sudo pacman -S paru
(yay is an equivalent alternative.)

column1: Downgrade an AUR package to a specific older version?
column2:
paru --getpkgbuild <pkg>   # clones the recipe into ./<pkg>
cd <pkg>
# edit PKGBUILD: pkgver=<old>  (and any hardcoded version in source=())
sudo pacman -S --needed pacman-contrib   # provides updpkgsums
updpkgsums                 # recompute checksums for the new file
makepkg -si                # build + install
# then pin it so -Syu won't bump it: IgnorePkg in /etc/pacman.conf

column1: pacman/paru: a prompt says 'There are N providers available for X' — what do you pick?
column2:
It's asking which repo to pull a shared dependency from. The providers are
equivalent -- press the default (1) or Enter. Not a real decision.

column1: systemd: enable a service AND start it now, then check it?
column2:
sudo systemctl enable --now <name>   # start now + start at every boot
systemctl status <name>              # active? logs? PID?
sudo systemctl disable --now <name>  # stop now + don't start at boot

Without --now, enable only affects FUTURE boots.

column1: systemctl status shows 'Loaded: ... enabled; preset: disabled' -- what does that mean?
column2:
enabled  = the CURRENT state you set (will start at boot).
preset   = the DISTRO DEFAULT for this unit (here: off).
Your explicit enable overrides the preset. So this line = 'I turned it on;
the distro would have left it off.' Not a conflict.

column1: Arch: generate a locale like en_US.UTF-8 (there's no locales-all package)?
column2:
# uncomment the line in /etc/locale.gen, then generate:
sudo sed -i 's/^#\(en_US.UTF-8 UTF-8\)/\1/' /etc/locale.gen
sudo locale-gen

check with:  locale -a | grep -i en_US
KDE's Region KCM can't auto-generate on Arch -- this is the manual route.

column1: KDE: set the default terminal emulator from the CLI and apply it?
column2:
kwriteconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key TerminalApplication wezterm-here.desktop
kbuildsycoca6                # rebuild the desktop/service cache so KDE sees it
kreadconfig6 --file kdeglobals --group General --key TerminalApplication  # verify

Value is the .desktop FILENAME (resolved from ~/.local/share/applications),
not a raw command. Swapping terminals in the GUI can reset it to a bare
command string -- re-set via CLI if that happens.

column1: A .desktop launcher for a terminal: which Terminal= value, and what is %f?
column2:
Terminal=false   # the app IS a terminal; Terminal=true makes KDE launch it
                 # INSIDE another terminal and can swallow your Exec args.
Exec=wezterm start --cwd %f   # %f = the folder KDE passes ('Open Terminal Here')

Duplicate Exec= lines -> parser uses the first and behaviour is undefined:
keep exactly one.

column1: Relink a symlink that points at a DIRECTORY without nesting the new link inside it?
column2:
ln -sfn TARGET LINKNAME

-n / --no-dereference: treat an existing symlink-to-dir as a plain file and
REPLACE it. Plain `ln -sf` FOLLOWS the existing link and creates the new one
INSIDE the target dir (e.g. ~/.wezterm/.wezterm -> itself). -n only needed
when the target is a directory; -sf is fine for a file target.

column1: Switch a cloned repo's remote from HTTPS to SSH (so pushes use your key)?
column2:
git remote -v                       # see current urls
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:OWNER/REPO.git

Gotcha: it's easy to drop the OWNER/ segment -- github.com:repo.git (no owner)
is wrong. Verify with `git remote -v`, confirm with `git fetch`.

column1: SSH: correct permissions for ~/.ssh and its files (e.g. after copying keys off NTFS)?
column2:
chmod 700 ~/.ssh
find ~/.ssh -type f -exec chmod 600 {} +                                  # lock ALL first (safe for any private key)
find ~/.ssh -type f \( -name '*.pub' -o -name 'known_hosts*' \) -exec chmod 644 {} +  # relax non-secrets

NTFS has no unix perms -> everything copies as 0755 -> 'bad permissions,
key ignored'. Private keys MUST be 600, the dir 700.

column1: WezTerm: one config file for BOTH Windows and Linux -- how to branch on OS?
column2:
local is_windows = wezterm.target_triple:find("windows") ~= nil

-- a table literal can't hold an `if`, so compute the OS-varying values as
-- locals ABOVE the return, then reference them inside the table:
local default_prog, launch_menu
if is_windows then default_prog = { "...bash.exe" } ; launch_menu = {...}
else                default_prog = { "/usr/bin/zsh", "-l" } ; launch_menu = {...} end
return { default_prog = default_prog, launch_menu = launch_menu, --[[...]] }

column1: AMD Ryzen desktop: random INSTANT-OFF reboots at idle, no blue screen (Kernel-Power 41, BugcheckCode 0). BIOS fix?
column2:
Deep CPU C-states drop power draw so low the PSU can't hold the rail at idle
-> instant power loss, nothing logged. It is NOT necessarily a dead PSU
(stress-testing stays stable; idle dies).

BIOS -> Advanced -> AMD CBS:
  Global C-state Control        = Disabled   (the reliable one)
  Power Supply Idle Control     = Typical Current Idle   (if the AGESA exposes it)
Windows stopgap: High Performance plan + disable sleep.
